scope: Separate native-intake source, target, license, reserved-metadata and bounded-reading provenance only.
conclusions: All declared native-intake artifact hashes checked against validation.json match.
The metadata view contains exactly 147 unchanged reserved rows and one new wholly-development markdown-it source. Neither that source hash nor either declared target hash matches reserved metadata.

The existing offline reference-context validator accepts the complete pinned 174-entry Git inventory, the one source and exactly two present targets. All source/target SHA-256, Git blob identities, sizes and line counts match.

The selected ten-line docs/README.md reproduces exactly two eligible local Markdown references, to docs/architecture.md and docs/development.md, plus its two resolver exclusions at the declared coordinates.

The original root README declaration and result remain byte-for-byte unchanged from their recorded commits: zero eligible references, 53 exclusions and no required targets. Its corpus bytes were not reopened in this audit.
The retained MIT LICENSE has its declared SHA-256, matches the pinned LICENSE blob identity, and preserves its copyright, permission and warranty text.
All thirteen saved reading files match their rendered hashes and embedded text; each remains within 80 physical lines and 80 Unicode code points per line.

Both canonical context/bundle hashes match. The existing context-reading builder reproduces the whole bundle exactly, and the focus/source rows and both target row sets reconstruct the complete original bytes without gaps or altered line endings.
No actionable engineering provenance defect was identified within this audit scope.
limits: This is engineering provenance evidence from an agent. It provides no independent human issue labels, clean annotations, calibration, usefulness assessment, precision/recall or population-effectiveness metric.
The commits establish declaration-to-binding ordering and exact frozen content. Historical first source/target byte-read timing cannot be independently proven from Git alone.
Normalized cross-split duplication remains unknown because reserved bytes were not opened.
The original root README result was checked for committed preservation and declared counts, rather than re-enumerated from its source cache.
The helper-based reproduction checks reproducibility and bindings; it is not an independent semantic evaluation of the rule.
The whole-package runtime digest and other-agent reviews were outside this audit and were not read or used.

development_source.attribution: Vitaly Puzrin, Alex Kocharin and markdown-it contributors
development_source.transformation: none; complete pinned UTF-8 Markdown source

selection_commit_evidence.proof_limit: Committed declarations precede later committed bindings; historical first byte-read timing is not independently observable from Git.

new_corpus_source_cache_reads.purpose: one existing validator read and one existing reading-builder read

exposure.display_event: An initial shape-inspection command printed nested reading-row maps, including source/target text, instead of only row counts. The tool truncated its 28,184-token output. Later verification emitted only metadata and hashes. This exposure involved only the already declared development source and its two targets.
exposure.temporary_writes: The existing native validator materialized only its one source and two targets in its disposable context directory and removed it. The additional resolver root remained empty.
exposure.previous_helper_context: Previously inspected native-reference, native-link and named production extraction/resolver helper code was retained from the earlier assigned audit; it was not reread for this scope.
exposure.open_audit_limit: Absolute corpus opens were restricted to the three declared byte paths plus their ancestor directories. The existing validator reads its bound source/targets through relative directory-descriptor opens, which are recorded separately.

failures.inspection_output_truncation: The initial nested row-map dump exceeded the requested output budget; this did not affect subsequent verification or page-bound checks.

summary: Inspected only native-intake declarations, metadata, retained license and existing helpers.
Recomputed artifact/input hashes, reserved metadata equality and commit-content ordering.
Ran the existing offline reference-context validator and an independent empty-root extraction.
Rebuilt the reading bundle with the existing builder, checked all 13 saved page hashes/bounds, and reconstructed all original source/target bytes.
Recorded exact helper identities and validated the final JSON and unchanged input file hashes.
